headline: High: shared filesystem plus broad shell/MCP in Goose creates dangerous write-conflict and cascading-error pathways with Copilot’s editable repo context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open buffers, while Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, so a malicious file or extension output from Goose can be surfaced into Copilot’s trusted context. Copilot lacks a documented provenance filter; Goose’s shared-state-via-filesystem makes the bridge plausible by default.
conditions: IF Goose writes attacker-controlled instructions into a file that Copilot later opens or indexes
IF Copilot treats repo context or open buffers as trusted instructions
mitigations: Restrict Copilot to a read-only branch or copy of the repo
Disable Goose MCP extensions for the shared workspace
Add a manual review step before Copilot consumes Goose-written files
Use separate directories for each agent's working files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, and Goose touches source code plus files in cwd with broad filesystem access. Even without explicit secret-handling fields, the shared workspace creates a realistic path for one agent to expose sensitive code or notes into the other agent’s outputs.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or notes are present in the shared workspace
IF Goose or Copilot outputs file contents into chat or generated edits
mitigations: Separate sensitive files into a directory only one agent can access
Run both agents on a sanitized test copy of the repo
Disable automatic inclusion of cwd files in Goose sessions
Review generated diffs before sharing them between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state; Goose also has shell, subprocess, install, and MCP capabilities, while Copilot can propose edits in Workspace. With Goose’s filesystem-shared concurrency and no locking shown, concurrent edits and git-state races are dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or working tree
IF Goose applies edits or shell-driven changes while Copilot Workspace also proposes edits
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees for isolation
Require manual merge review after each agent run

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot’s Workspace plans and applies edits, and Goose can act through shell/MCP with user confirmation. If Goose-generated code or instructions are fed into Copilot, or Copilot’s edits are then executed by Goose, errors can cascade into real actions or committed changes without strong verification.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated edits are passed to Goose for execution or follow-up automation
IF Goose treats Copilot output as authoritative without independent validation
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Disable Goose execution on Copilot-authored files
Limit Goose to read-only analysis for Copilot outputs
Require tests or lint checks before any applied edit is accepted

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are vendor-documented coding agents with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch fields. Copilot’s GitHub repo OAuth and Goose’s model-provider keys imply different handling paths, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict, so only a low, documentation-gap risk is supportable.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated data through a provider path with stricter residency or retention rules
IF the operator stores regulated data in the shared workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review provider DPAs and retention settings before use
Use synthetic or redacted data for joint runs
Document which agent may process which data class
